content.text: The spatial results from round 4 show that the water front on the I12-W to P16 path has advanced toward the producer, while the rise in water production still lags the historical response. I will add a control that changes only porosity on this path, holding permeability and composition fixed, to test whether reducing storage volume can improve breakthrough timing. I will draw the conclusion after rerunning the entire history.

Round 5 passed the original simulator's input checks. Permeability, initial composition, and the other fixed inputs agree with round 4. Only the porosity of the designated path changed, and the initial fractions still sum to 1 in every cell. The simulation is progressing. I will report errors for the field and all six wells side by side and identify which wells improve and which deteriorate.

The porosity control shows a partial-period response consistent with the hypothesis. Over the first 1439 days, lowering only the porosity on the I12-W to P16 path reduced P16 water-rate RMSE from 59.73 to 53.10 m³/d. The other wells show essentially the same response. The improvement so far is limited. I still need to check the later rise in water rate and the full-period error.

The effect of the porosity control is clearer over the first 1789 days. P16 water-rate RMSE fell from 180.85 in round 4 to 96.52 m³/d, and field oil/water RMSE fell from 289.94 to 226.26 m³/d. The other well responses changed very little. The P16 water rate at day 1789 was already slightly above history, so I still need to check for overproduction of water later on.

Round 5 continued to improve the P16 match over the first 2119 days. Water-rate RMSE fell from 230.15 in round 4 to 128.96 m³/d. At day 2119 the water rate was 916 m³/d against a historical 1034 m³/d. Field oil/water RMSE also fell from 345.89 to 254.76 m³/d. The other wells essentially retained their previous response. I will continue validating the final 772 days.

All three candidates have now completed 2891 days and 516 report steps. I am calculating the complete round 5 score and cross-checking the final inputs, the actual forward-simulation arrays, and the source hashes. I will then select the candidate using the full-period metrics fixed in advance.

The complete results confirm round 5 as the best candidate. Field oil-rate and water-rate RMSE each fell to about 545 m³/d. Combined NRMSE was 11.62%, and full-period error at all six wells was lower than with the original fields. The end-of-history P16 water rate is still 1318 m³/d, below the historical 2192 m³/d. The delivery materials will document this mismatch.

The full-period history-matching experiment is complete, covering **2891 days and 516 report steps**. Round 5 was selected.

- Field oil-rate and water-rate RMSE each fell from approximately **2089.43 to 544.72 m³/d**, a **73.93%** reduction.
- The combined field and well NRMSE fell from **37.98% to 11.62%**. All six wells had lower full-period error than with the original fields.

The selected match changed only porosity and permeability. The initial five-component composition retained its original normalized values and sums to 1 in every cell. The source hashes for the simulator and its key dependencies were verified.

**A substantial mismatch remains at P16.** Its end-of-history water rate was 1318 m³/d, well below the historical 2192 m³/d.
